questions.prompt: The team deploys manually on Thursday nights and it usually goes badly. What changes the most, soonest?
options: A dedicated release manager to run the deploys.
A pipeline that builds one artifact, tests it, and ships that same artifact to staging then production.
questions.explanation: Manual deploys go wrong because they're different every time. One tested artifact promoted through environments removes the variable. Moving the day helps a little — at least someone's awake to fix it — but it's treating the symptom. Kubernetes is a much larger change that doesn't address why the deploy is unrepeatable.

questions.prompt: A production deployment fails its post-deploy smoke test.

items.text: Preserve logs and deployment metadata for diagnosis
Stop progression and roll back or shift traffic to the last known-good version
Confirm user-facing recovery and key health signals
Investigate the failure and add a prevention or detection improvement

questions.explanation: Restore service first, confirm recovery, preserve evidence, then investigate and improve the system. Debugging while users remain on a known-bad release extends the incident unnecessarily.
